reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact native source, enlarged source page 11 and targeted source panel, complete unchanged full native RGBA raw, targeted native-resolution beard/pose and returned-note crops, full white/cyan/alpha sheet and unchanged naiwa mascot reference

remaining_reasons: The source head is turned toward image left with a down-left gaze. The return reverses the head orientation toward image right with a forward/right gaze, changing the visible eye sizes, nose/mouth orientation and cheek plane. Restore the source image-left three-quarter pose and down-left gaze.

The source cream note has existing compact upper gray marks and only a small dark right-edge tab. The return removes those upper gray marks entirely and invents a large dark metal clip across the note's upper edge. Remove the clip and restore the source's compact upper-mark footprint while retaining the cream paper and original tab.
entries.positive_observation: Dark brushed-back hair, dark eyebrows and thin rectangular spectacles remain. A separate dark-grey upper-lip moustache and a short grey beard connect across the chin and along both lower-jaw curves; the upper central cheeks around the spectacles remain yellow, and the deep side shading was not mistaken for an additional beard defect. One sober closed mouth and the plain dark navy-black close-collared garment remain. The rounded lower head meets the collar without a separate long stalk. The complete dark tilted frame and opaque dark blue-grey photographic backing remain, and full white/cyan comparisons show no visible holes, lost backing or working-matte ring. The reversed pose and replaced note content are the clear rejection reasons above.
entries.visible_limitations: Fine spectacle rims, individual beard hairs, obscured garment details and note lettering are not reliably readable at 65x67. The beard was checked by its visible overall boundary rather than individual hairs; no extra beard rejection is claimed. Pose reversal and complete loss/replacement of the note marks are clearly visible.
